newsitem.title: USA: BOE's George urges caution on stable forex pledges.
newsitem.headline: BOE's George urges caution on stable forex pledges.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George cautioned major nations on Monday against promising more currency stability than they can deliver.
"Frustrating though it is, we should be cautious in promising greater exchange rate stability than we can deliver," George told the International Monetary Fund's Interim Committee.
He said that the pursuit of stable monetary and fiscal policies "undoubtedly" would make a major contribution to ensuring currency stability.

"By and large, the directions of movements in exchange rates over the last couple of years ... appear to be consistent with (a) picture of healthy growth, insofar as they are helping to achieve a better economic balance between the major regions," George said.
But he added that he could not be "entirely comfortable" with the very large currency gyrations of the past.
"There is a risk that the healthy correction of earlier misalignments could now be carried too far in some cases," George said.
George was generally upbeat about the outlook for the world economy, but said that there were risks.
"In the U.S., the duration of the expansion makes it difficult to decide when to tighten policy further to head off any danger of overheating," George said.
"And in the U.K., there is a need, in setting policy, to strike a balance between the strong growth of domestic demand and the recent sharp appreciation of the exchange rate," he added.
